dedupe_keys.name: insurance council of australia data hub historical normalised catastrophe list

description: Insurance Council of Australia (ICA) publishes the insurance industry's record of declared natural-hazard catastrophes and significant events in Australia, with a downloadable Historical Normalised Catastrophe list (updated July 2026) whose records the page says go back to 1967, plus per-event pages giving claims count, claims incurred, outstanding claims and the share of claims closed (for example Catastrophe 261, the Victoria bushfires: 4.85 thousand claims, 598 million incurred, 81.9 per cent closed as at July 2026). Coverage: Australia, insured losses of events declared as catastrophes or significant events by the ICA, from member insurers' reports; the list is described as normalised, which is not defined on the page read. Format and access: an XLSX workbook download and HTML event summaries, free and without registration from the ICA Data Hub. Licence (read on the portal page on 2026-09-29): Proprietary: ICA Data Hub disclaimer (non-commercial use with attribution to the ICA; commercial exploitation not permitted; all rights reserved); cost: free. Caveats: the data are a summary of insurers' reports, so uninsured damage is absent and the page disclaims accuracy and completeness; the workbook was not opened, so its columns and the normalisation method are unconfirmed; use is limited to non-commercial purposes with attribution. Simulation uses: calibrating flood, bushfire and storm loss and vulnerability models for housing, testing insured-damage estimates against declared events, and building event catalogues for building-stock resilience studies. Related catalogue records: OpenStreetMap (data-openstreetmap).
